implication: Regulation 31(4) filings are post-transaction disclosures and do not require prior SEBI approval; they serve as notice to the market that a shareholding threshold has been breached—a key distinction from Section 4 (prior intimation) in M&A structuring for cross-border group consolidations.

sum: Spanish-domiciled entity linked to CIE Automotive group made a substantial acquisition in listed CIE Automotive India Limited, triggering mandatory Regulation 31(4) disclosure under SEBI's takeover code. The filing indicates a shareholding milestone was crossed, though the exact percentage and consideration remain undisclosed in publicly available sources.
detail: Participaciones Internacionales Autometal DOS, S.L., a Spanish entity, submitted a mandatory disclosure to NSE under Regulation 31(4) of the SEBI (Substantial Acquisition of Shares and Takeovers) Regulations, 2011, indicating acquisition of shares in CIE Automotive India Limited. CIE Automotive is a global automotive components supplier with listed operations in India. The disclosure was filed on 8 May 2026, per NSE archives. No prior intimation (Regulation 4) filings are visible, suggesting either the acquisition occurred via open market or a negotiated block purchase below the 5% threshold initially, with the disclosure filing marking the moment a material threshold was crossed.
